hypothesis: Learned cross-encounter relational persistence can reject coincident witness impostors under novel graph structures better than strongest equal-evidence consensus.

candidate_mechanism.input: Per-encounter observed relation witnesses, anonymous encounter identifiers and edge roles, never semantic/canonical identity or evaluation answers
candidate_mechanism.learning: Small fixed-capacity train-only scorer of persistence across encounters; readout trained on disjoint entity IDs
candidate_mechanism.identification: Search candidate endpoint pairs, not supplied alias tuples
candidate_mechanism.history_cost_accounting: All outside-core encounter storage, observations and candidate search comparisons must be measured and reported separately; any unmetered external lookup is INVALID
candidate_mechanism.independence: One generated encounter must not reuse a source truth hint or deterministic ID encoding as its join evidence

evaluation.generation_contract: new generator independent from F28's motif 108-111 and witnesses; exact generator SHA, seeds and hashes must be frozen before original

matched_controls: equal measured history bytes and read operations or explicit cost-normalized comparison
audit: per-case truth and all arm predictions

advance_rule.impostor_false_positives: strictly fewer than strongest fair control
advance_rule.genuine_true_positives: no drop greater than one percentage point
advance_rule.invalid_if_any: source identity drift; leaked identity; oracle inconsistency; missed cost accounting; changed threshold after freeze
